newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Q4 current account, GDP data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Q4 current account, GDP data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK current account and final GDP data for the fourth quarter of 1996:

"I guess there was a fear in the market there would be an upward revision to these (GDP) numbers given the data we've seen of late... On the current account it's a very good number. We've yet to see any deterioration in the trade position arising from sterling's appreciation. To that extent it's probably a small positive for sterling."

"Essentially, these numbers confirm the picture given by the first revision -- namely that output is growing above trend, but not worringly so. Markets should not currently fear a narrowing of the output gap."

"The GDP figures are very much in line with expectations and show the economy is being led by consumer sales. The most encouraging aspect is the pick up in investment which may finally show that investment may finally be responding to higher demand."
"The current account figures are surprisingly good and overall they should give sterling some underpinning."

"The economy seems to be growing at a fairly healthy pace and the markets are fearful rates could rise after the election, but I still think if Labour get in they're going to tighten fiscal policy and so rates wouldn't need to rise by very much."
